books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Secession dates verified against the Ordinance of Secession table (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordinance_of_Secession), the American Battlefield Trust Civil War timeline (battlefields.org), and Digital History, University of Houston (digitalhistory.uh.edu). Texas adopted its ordinance February 1, 1861, confirmed by popular referendum February 23; Virginia's ordinance was ratified by referendum May 23, 1861.
stimulus.text:
Ordinances of secession, in the order the states adopted them. Seven states seceded before Lincoln's inauguration on March 4, 1861; four more followed after the firing on Fort Sumter.

| State | Date of ordinance |
| South Carolina | December 20, 1860 |
| Mississippi | January 9, 1861 |
| Florida | January 10, 1861 |
| Alabama | January 11, 1861 |
| Georgia | January 19, 1861 |
| Louisiana | January 26, 1861 |
| Texas | February 1, 1861 |
| Virginia | April 17, 1861 |
| Arkansas | May 6, 1861 |
| Tennessee | May 6, 1861 |
| North Carolina | May 20, 1861 |

Delaware, Kentucky, Maryland, and Missouri were slave states that stayed in the Union and are not listed.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: According to the table, which state was the first to secede?

options.misconception: Virginia's ordinance came April 17, 1861, months after the first secession.
Mississippi seceded January 9, 1861, twenty days after South Carolina.
Texas adopted its ordinance February 1, 1861, the last of the first seven.

rationales.A: Virginia's ordinance came April 17, 1861, months after the first secession.
rationales.B: Mississippi seceded January 9, 1861, twenty days after South Carolina.
rationales.C: The table lists South Carolina first, with an ordinance dated December 20, 1860 — weeks before any other state.
rationales.D: Texas adopted its ordinance February 1, 1861, the last of the first seven.
rationales.general:
1. Read the table top to bottom: the dates run in order.
2. December 20, 1860 is the earliest date on the list.
3. Background: South Carolina's convention voted unanimously, and six states followed within six weeks.
4. First matters, because the first state tested whether secession would be answered.
Remember: in a dated list, the earliest date is the answer — do not let a famous name later in the list pull you forward.
